ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Question: Consider a silicon sample at \( T = 300 \, K \), with a uniform donor density \( N_d = 5 \times 10^{16} \, \text{cm}^{-3} \) illuminated uniformly such that the optical generation rate is \( G_{\text{opt}} = 1.5 \times 10^{20} \, \text{cm}^{-3} \text{s}^{-1} \) throughout the sample. The incident radiation is turned off at \( t = 0 \). Assume low-level injection to be valid and ignore surface effects. The carrier lifetimes are \( \tau_{p0} = 0.1 \, \mu s \) and \( \tau_{n0} = 0.5 \, \mu s \).

The hole concentration at \( t = 0 \) and the hole concentration at \( t = 0.3 \, \mu s \), respectively, are:
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Hole Concentration at t = 0.3 μs

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Given Gopt = 1.5 × 10^20 cm^-3 s^-1, τp0 = 0.1 μs, and the target time t = 0.3 μs. Convert the hole lifetime: τp0 = 0.1 μs = 1 × 10^-7 s. Under low-level injection, the steady-state excess hole concentration just before the light is turned off is Δp(0) = Gopt τp0 = (1.5 × 10^20)(1 × 10^-7) = 1.5 × 10^13 cm^-3. After the radiation is turned off, the excess hole concentration decays exponentially: Δp(t) = Δp(0)e^(-t/τp0). Here t/τp0 = 0.3 μs / 0.1 μs = 3. Therefore Δp(0.3 μs) = 1.5 × 10^13 e^-3 = 7.47 × 10^11 cm^-3. The equilibrium minority hole concentration is negligible compared with this value, so the hole concentration is approximately 7.47 × 10^11 cm^-3.

method.method_draft: Let p0 be the thermal equilibrium hole concentration. Before t=0, steady state gives 0=Gopt-(p(0)-p0)/τp0, so p(0)=p0+Gopt τp0. After switch-off, solve dp/dt=-(p-p0)/τp0 with this initial value: p(t)=p0+[p(0)-p0]e^-t/τp0=p0+Gopt τp0 e^-t/τp0. Estimate p0=ni^2/Nd if desired; at 300 K it is many orders below 10^12 cm^-3, so neglect it. Insert Gopt=1.5×10^20 cm^-3 s^-1, τp0=0.1 μs=10^-7 s, and t=0.3 μs to obtain p≈1.5×10^13 e^-3=7.47×10^11 cm^-3.
